speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Being a parent to Ella, Katie and Poppy has been one of the greatest joys for my wife Amy and I.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I share so many stories of them because I am so grateful that I have three happy, healthy children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am grateful for all the lessons they have taught me and they have undoubtedly made me a better person.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I love and treasure them so much and I want to share the joys of being a parent with everyone.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Amy and I fought very hard to have children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There was a point in our lives when we could not have kids.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The story I have shared less is that we were able to have our three children only with the help of in-vitro fertilisation, or IVF.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Going through IVF was like being on an emotional roller coaster ride.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When we were undergoing IVF, I was taking home a salary of about $2,000 a month.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We had to pour all our income and savings towards having a child.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Like us, many couples have struggled to conceive.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Fertility is an existential problem in Singapore and the Government has done much, such as expanding the Baby Bonus Scheme, to provide more support to couples in their decision to have children and to lighten the financial costs of raising children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I do not think we are doing enough for those who want but struggle to have children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I met several such couples at a dialogue session I organised last November through the Singapore IVF Support Group.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The couples spoke candidly about the many challenges they faced and I thank them for sharing their personal stories and passionate recommendations with me.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Today, I will share their stories with you and offer four proposals on how the Government can help couples like them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first proposal is for the Government to subsidise more cycles of IVF.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Each cycle, each roll of the dice, can cost up to $15,000 at our public hospitals.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Government does help with subsidies for six cycles.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Starting from the seventh cycle, you pay the full unsubsidised amount.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is a painful reality for many couples.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One couple I met are Josephine and Winston.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They have gone through nine IVF cycles, paying about $20,000 out-of-pocket and $15,000 via MediSave already.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Today, they are still without a child and will continue to try.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Another couple I met are Cheryl and Keith.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: By their sixth cycle, the very last subsidised IVF cycle, they managed to conceive and are now happy parents to a bubbly one-year-old.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But they now find themselves in an agonising position of wanting a second child.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They wonder: can we really afford to go through IVF unsubsidised?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I should pause here and clarify that nobody chooses to do a seventh cycle of IVF unless they have to.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Each cycle involves mood-changing medication, weeks of daily painful injections and multiple visits to the doctor.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am not proposing that we extend subsidies to unlimited cycles of IVF.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I propose that we extend subsidies to the seventh and eighth IVF cycles.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If needed, we can reduce the subsidies for these cycles to ensure that the scheme remains sustainable.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This was done about seven years ago and it is time for us to review this again.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If the argument is that most couples have a successful pregnancy before or during their sixth cycle, then extending subsidies to the seventh and eighth cycle would not cost the Government much.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should remember that this additional subsidy is meant for couples, such as Josephine, Winston, Cheryl and Keith, who have clearly shown, through years of trying, that they are serious about wanting to become parents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second proposal is to introduce subsidies for pre-implantation genetic diagnosis, or PGD, and allow the balance to be paid out of MediSave, subject to a limit.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: PGD is sometimes conducted during IVF cycles and it is important in two ways.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One, for couples with a family history of genetic disorders, it ensures that the embryo does not inherit serious medical conditions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Two, PGD increases the likelihood of a pregnancy being successful.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Studies done by researchers at the University of Valencia and at Japanese hospitals found that PGD significantly reduced miscarriages and increased the chances of pregnancy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This, of course, means happier outcomes for couples.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It might also mean lower costs for the Government, as fewer IVF cycles may be needed before a successful pregnancy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Yet, for all its benefits, not a single dollar of subsidy or MediSave is available for PGD.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For Amelia and Geoffrey, paying $18,000 for PGD was the only way to prevent their second child from inheriting a rare genetic disease that can lead to liver failure.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Another couple, Sophia and John, had already faced three miscarriages.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They found that a genetic condition was at fault and had to pay $10,000 for PGD to prevent more miscarriages and to avoid birth defects.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope the numbers are as big a shock for Members of this House as they were for these couples.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For Singaporean couples, this means a 75% subsidy for PGD for subsidised IVF cycles.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: PGD is needed only by a small percentage of couples.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, overall subsidy costs for the Government are likely to be limited.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should also allow PGD to be paid using MediSave, subject to a cap, so that MediSave does not get exhausted by such procedures.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is already the case for IVF treatments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Couples deserve their chance to have healthy children and we should support them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Currently, the Government's subsidy of six IVF cycles comes with a condition: three of the cycles must be "fresh" and the other three must be "frozen".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I will spare this House the scientific nitty-gritty of what "fresh" and "frozen" mean.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But suffice to say, expert opinion is split and the medical literature is inconclusive about whether one is clearly better than the other.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Indeed, Minister Gan himself said last October, "The success rates for fresh and frozen eggs are largely comparable." Sir, I think this quota adds unnecessary stress on couples undergoing IVF.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some couples may need one fresh cycle and five frozen cycles while others may need five fresh cycles and one frozen cycle.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We simply provide subsidies for a given number of cycles, which can be either fresh or frozen.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Financial subsidies are important but providing people with precious time is also important.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I propose we introduce fertility leave for both husbands and wives to take time off work for IVF treatments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is particularly true for working women who have to juggle their career alongside the side effects and time commitments of their IVF treatments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: More than half found it difficult to take time off work for IVF-related treatments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The existing 14 days of sick leave is insufficient for them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some end up taking no-pay leave and this is a strain on their already tight budgets due to IVF.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As for men, I believe we want to be with our wife during these tough times.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When I spoke with Amelia and Geoffrey, Geoffrey told me that he wished he could take more time to accompany Amelia to her IVF appointments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But he cannot take medical leave to accompany his wife to these appointments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To ensure the leave is taken for its intended purpose, we can consider requiring employees to furnish MCs from fertility clinics and allow fertility clinics to provide men with MCs when they accompany their wife for their IVF appointments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition to allowing Singaporean women to more easily access IVF treatments, fertility leave also has two additional positive side effects.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: First, it could help with our fertility rates.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: South Korea, a country with fertility rates nearly identical to ours, introduced fertility treatment leave as part of their efforts to raise fertility rates.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, it makes clear that fertility treatments like IVF are not the concern of women alone.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The emotional support of their husbands is essential.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Just like parenting, conception should be a two-person job.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Over the years, we have introduced the co-funding scheme for IVF treatments, increased the co-funding to more cycles and also increased the co-funding limits.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We have also lifted the age limit of 45 years old for women to undergo IVF and extended IVF subsidies to women who are 40 years or older.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also raised the issue of pre-implantation genetic screenings, or PGS, previously and I am glad the Government has started a pilot for this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is also positive news that the Government is considering allowing IVF subsidies to be applied at private fertility treatment centres and is reviewing Government support for PGD and PGS.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But we can and we should do more.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These proposals will help more couples undergoing IVF and, most importantly, reduce their stress levels as they embark on this stressful but potentially rewarding IVF journey – potentially rewarding for the couples and also for Singapore as we try hard to increase our total fertility rate.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ella, Katie and Poppy bring us immeasurable joy every single day and, of course, to be honest, immeasurable pain at times as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My three little ones are, fortunately and unfortunately, as stubborn as me.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Recently, Poppy gave me a kiss in the morning and said, "I love you, daddy" and went back to sleep.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I sometimes find photos Katie has taken of herself on my phone without me knowing and some selfies she took together with me while I was asleep.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Those are the only photos on my phone when my centre parting is not perfectly dead-centre.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ella will pick up snails and caterpillars and move them off the pavement so nobody will step on them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As they said, "Teaching a child not to step on a caterpillar is as valuable to the child as it is to the caterpillar." Sir, I hope everyone will have the chance to experience these moments and to share these stories about their loved ones.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For Amy and I, as well as Josephine, Winston, Cheryl, Keith, Amelia, Geoffrey, Sophia and John, and many, many other couples, parenthood is a castle with high walls.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Nothing is so wonderful and daunting, heart-breaking and soul-lifting, taxing and exhilarating as raising a child.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And certainly nothing will stretch us, inspire us and motivate us to better ourselves quite like being the one that little person looks up to." I should also end by saying that I am not speaking up to get more subsidies so that I can have more children.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We share his concern on the importance of supporting couples with parenthood aspirations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This has always been a whole-of-Government priority for us and we will continue to work towards providing better support for couples in this journey.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: First, let me share some of the efforts made over the years to ensure greater affordability of assisted reproduction technology, or ART, for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The ART co-funding scheme, which was first introduced in 2008, aims to provide co-funding for ART treatments performed at public assisted reproduction, or AR centres – namely SGH, NUH or KKH – for couples where at least one spouse is a Singapore Citizen, or SC.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Since then, enhancements have been made progressively to better support couples with parenthood aspirations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: At that time, co-funding of 75% for up to three frozen cycles, capped at $1,200 per cycle, was also introduced.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Couples were hence able to benefit from co-funding of three fresh and three frozen cycles, or a total of six cycles.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: With effect from 1 January 2020, we further enhanced Government co-funding to allow up to two of the six existing co-funded ART cycles to occur after the women turned 40 as long as they have attempted assisted reproduction or intra-uterine insemination, or IUI, procedures before age 40.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Patients can also use MediSave to help offset the out-of-pocket payment at both public and private AR centres.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: There is no cap on the number of cycles and patients may use up to $6,000 for the first cycle, $5,000 for the second cycle and $4,000 for the third and subsequent cycles.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These withdrawal limits are designed to strike a balance between supporting couples with their costs of treatment today and helping them conserve funds for their healthcare needs in retirement.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: After co-funding and MediSave usage for the first cycle, eight in 10 eligible SC couples would incur no out-of-pocket expense while nine in 10 eligible SC couples could expect to pay no more than $500.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Couples who find themselves unable to cope with unexpectedly large bills – for instance, as a result of complications – even after co-funding, may appeal to use MediSave beyond the current limits to pay for treatment.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Such appeals will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I trust Mr Ng would appreciate that as much as we would like to help as many couples with their parenthood aspirations, we also need to balance the need to meaningfully and responsibly allocate public funds on this.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As we work on improving the affordability of ART, we must continue our evidence-based approach to guide our co-funding eligibility criteria.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Clinical evidence has shown that the success rate for ART carried out beyond age 40 decreases significantly, with the probability of pregnancy complications also increasing with maternal age.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: While the success rate is low in women aged 40 years and above, we acknowledge that there are still successful cases.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is not just a matter of Government funding but the strain of couples to keep trying.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Hence, we must continue to encourage couples to marry and start families early in order to maximise the chances of conception.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For those who have challenges, we will continue to build a support eco-system for them, but co-funding needs to be feasible and take into account clinical efficacy.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Ng has requested to introduce co-funding for more ART cycles beyond the existing limit of six cycles.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Currently, the number of co-funded ART cycles is set at three fresh and three frozen cycles based on clinical evidence, which shows that the success rate of ART decreases with age as each successive cycle progresses.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I appreciate Mr Ng's suggestion and understand where he is coming from.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: At the same time, we should continue to stay grounded by the clinical evidence regarding the efficacy of ART for successive cycles to ensure that Government funding is used in a cost-effective way.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It may be useful to note that amongst the women who successfully achieve pregnancy, these women undergo an average of two AR cycles before doing so.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I accept though that this is an emotional process and couples may want to keep trying.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Couples can, nevertheless, continue to tap on their MediSave up to the $15,000 lifetime limit.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will monitor the clinical evidence and review the criteria if new data suggests improved outcomes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Ng also suggested to provide co-funding for preimplantation genetic diagnosis, or PGD, of up to 75% within the six ART cycles.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: PGD is currently offered to patients at risk of transmitting serious inheritable diseases that are due to single gene mutations or chromosomal structural rearrangements at around $10,000 to $19,000 per cycle.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: A pilot study on PGD conducted by NUH has found some evidence that PGD is able to lower the risk of serious disease in the child as well as increase the likelihood of carrying the child to term.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: PGD, indeed, appears to have benefits which could lead to better outcomes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: However, the cost of the procedure is high.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We note Mr Ng's argument that subsidising PGD may mean lower costs for the Government as fewer IVF cycles may be needed before a successful pregnancy.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will release more details on this review when ready.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Meanwhile, patients continue to be supported by co-funding of other associated costs, such as for AR treatments.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: One other suggestion raised by Mr Ng was to provide flexibility for couples to choose between fresh and frozen cycles for the six co-funded ART cycles.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Co-funding for three fresh and three frozen cycles is a considered approach that allows couples to freeze and store excess embryos produced from fresh cycles and to follow up with a frozen treatment cycle subsequently.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Co-funding had, in the past, been limited to three fresh cycles only as previous assessments showed that fresh cycles had significantly higher success rates than frozen cycles.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: However, we understand that, from a clinical perspective, going for more fresh cycles can potentially increase the risks of ovarian hyper stimulation, which is a known complication of fresh cycles.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As the success rates for frozen ART cycles improved over the years and were close to that of fresh cycles in 2009 and 2010, the decision was hence made to extend co-funding to three frozen cycles instead of introducing more fresh cycles to encourage couples to use their frozen embryos left over from previous fresh cycles so that they will not need to go through fresh cycles again just to be eligible for co-funding.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Co-funding a permutation of three fresh and three frozen cycles is expected to be more cost-effective than six fresh cycles as the charges for a frozen cycle is lower than that of a fresh cycle and the success rates of both options are expected to be comparable.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Nevertheless, I agree with Mr Ng that some couples might have different preferences and needs and may, for instance, wish to utilise more frozen cycles instead of fresh cycles.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MOH recognises this and is able to cater to such situations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Couples may approach MOH to request to tap on their unutilised co-funding for fresh or frozen cycles.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, a patient who has utilised one fresh cycle and three frozen cycles can request for co-funding for an additional frozen cycle since there are two unutilised fresh cycles remaining.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The co-funding would be capped based on the limit for frozen cycles and the patient would then have one remaining fresh cycle.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Similarly, a patient who has utilised one frozen cycle and three fresh cycles can utilise their co-funding for an additional fresh cycle since there are two unutilised frozen cycles remaining.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The co-funding would also be capped based on the limit for frozen cycles and the patient would then have one remaining unutilised frozen cycle.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Ng has proposed gender-neutral fertility leave for the couple undergoing assisted conception procedures based on the issuance of a Medical Certificate.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Today, women who are undergoing ACPs are entitled to hospitalisation leave, given their medically-invasive nature.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This allows them to take time off work to attend the treatments and get proper rest after.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Some doctors also provide husbands who accompany their wives for oocyte retrieval or embryo transfer with memos, which certain employers recognise by extending a day off.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In extending or introducing leave schemes, we should avoid inadvertently affecting the employability of individuals who use it.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: What is clear though is that all parties can benefit from greater flexibility at the workplace.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I encourage employers to be understanding and supportive of their employees, both women as well as their husbands, who are undergoing ART.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This could include allowing employees time-off or allowing husbands to work from home to be by their wife's side as she recuperates.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Parenthood indeed brings immeasurable joy, as the experiences Mr Ng shared about his "castle" show us.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: However, some unfortunately face difficulties in achieving the hopes of becoming parents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We understand how emotional and challenging the journey can be.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The suite of measures that have been rolled out over the years bears testament to how policies are continually reviewed to keep pace with new clinical evidence and achieve more effective outcomes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: While we may not be able to meet the demands of each and every couple, we will continue to do our part in providing the best support we can and adopt a balanced, evidence-based approach to serve our citizens better.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Once again, I thank Mr Ng for his suggestions and hope that we can continue to work together on this front.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Ng, you have got less than three minutes for clarifications and that includes Ms Rahayu Mahzam's reply.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: One, I thank the Parliamentary Secretary for sharing that they are going to review subsidies for PGD.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can I just ask how long this review will take and when we can expect the results?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Two, just wondering whether we will review the number of subsidised IVF cycles again?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: If something comes up and it is something that we can review, we will consider the proposals that you have made.
